title: The catering problem
narration: Axion Kitchen: quantum optimization for catering production. This is batch-production scheduling: cookers are machines, cleaning is setup work, and departures are due dates. We choose quantities, shared allocations, resources and phase times under freshness limits, qualified workers and calendars. Urgent orders and outages trigger replanning while started work stays fixed. Complete meals come first, then waste, batches and changes.

title: Batch selection and scheduling constraints
narration: A bit selects one locally valid batch, not a solved kitchen schedule. It fixes quantity, allocations, resources and times. Anchor blocks preserve compatible offered subsets; cross-block penalties exclude clashes. In the code, product expands coverage products; the coefficient span plus one sets a safe penalty. title: Complete meals and food waste
narration: Main coverage times side coverage gives complete service; their sum minus twice the product counts unpaired food. Both coverages are linear in batch bits, so the objective stays quadratic. Each priority weight dominates all lower costs combined. For hard constraints, P equals the full objective coefficient span plus one. A violation therefore cannot beat any feasible schedule. This guarantees feasible ground states, not heuristic convergence.
live_action: Explain MS and waste first; after 60% the screen shows the range bound and penalty inequality. State the ground-state guarantee.
live_narration: Linear main and side coverage multiply into quadratic service and waste terms. Priority weights dominate lower costs. For hard constraints, the objective range is at most S. Set P to S plus one: every invalid state costs more than every feasible state. That proves the ground-state guarantee.
shot: Paired-coverage truth table, then the actual penalty-bound argument.
editor_cue: At 60% switch to the proof. Define S over the full bit domain, show P=S+1 and E(invalid)≥E(feasible)+1. A heuristic need not reach a ground state; R=B here.

title: QAOA results
narration: We selected the QAOA configuration on the cell and S0/S1. On held-out S2/S3, it finds the offered-pool optimum in all ten seeds at both budgets. Random-angle search also hits all ten on S2. At two hundred fifty-six evaluations, median optimum probability per shot is about eleven and twenty-two times random-angle search. Angles are optimized per instance. These restricted portfolios still exclude better full-grid schedules.

title: VQE comparison
narration: VQE uses one-hot Givens gates and controlled rotations between coupled blocks. With exact CVaR and adjoint gradients, median optimum probability is about twelve percent on both held-out cases. That exceeds our QAOA probability, but parameter counts, training budgets and final shots differ. The primary VQE setup hits ten of ten and nine of ten seeds.
live_narration: VQE concentrates about twelve percent probability on the optimum in both cases. Its budgets and shot count differ from QAOA, so we show the methods separately.

title: VeloxQ: remove idle bits
narration: VeloxQ searches larger QUBOs of the same production model. Removing redundant idle bits preserves feasible schedules and their objective. At equal twenty-thousand-step budgets, the best checked plan serves fifty meals instead of ten, out of one hundred forty. Waste rises from thirty to sixty portions: complete service has priority. Valid returns rise from seventeen to all five hundred twelve. This is one exploratory job per representation; classical controls still find better plans.

live_narration: For VeloxQ, proved idle elimination improves the best plan from ten to fifty meals served at the same step budget. Waste increases; our objective prioritizes service. Valid returns rise from seventeen to five hundred twelve. Classical controls still find better plans.

editor_cue: Keep 20,000 steps and single-job scope visible. Waste rises 30→60 portions because service has priority. Same source programs/objective, different sampling matrices; CP/SA still better.

title: What makes the choices difficult?
narration: The cell is deliberately small. Larger inputs generate eighteen thousand batch programs. Equipment, workers and paired demand couple their choices. We measure restriction loss and search quality separately.
live_narration: Small cells test correctness. Larger inputs generate eighteen thousand programs with shared-resource conflicts. More variables alone do not establish hardness; benchmarks show quality and runtime.
